subject.declared_domain: NFRA_GLOBGRPH Item-3 -- THE canonical projection loader. Reads the Iceberg graph_nodes + graph_edges tables at the Nessie branch head and projects them into a local Kuzu DB (CloudNode / CloudEdge) for cross-layer Cypher traversal. Unlike kuzu_load.py (snapshot-tarball, nodes only) it reads the tables themselves, so it includes incremental commits made since the last nightly snapshot, and it loads the EDGE set.

as_of.graph_vintage: Pins at RUN time to the branch-head marker s3://opal-313476888478-globgrph/warehouse/_branch_head.main.json, measured live this session at LastModified 2026-08-30T02:11:47Z -- ~46 min before carding, and 2 s before the AWS snapshot tarball (02:11:49Z) that its sibling producer reads. The marker names the graph_nodes / graph_edges metadata_location that the run actually loads.

methodology.how: main() reads the writer-stamped branch-head marker via _provenance.read_branch_head_marker() and takes the graph_nodes / graph_edges metadata_location from it (the HEAD oracle). If the marker is absent it prints WARN: HEAD-ORACLE UNKNOWN and falls back to latest_table_metadata(), a paginated newest-*.metadata.json-by-mtime scan. Each table is read whole through pyiceberg StaticTable.from_metadata(...).scan().to_arrow(). Nodes are deduped into `best` on the canonical key (arn if non-empty else node_id), keeping the highest snapshot_ts and COUNTING key collisions. With --force (the DEFAULT) the existing Kuzu DB is dropped -- file or directory, plus its .wal -- and a surviving path raises SystemExit rather than proceeding. Nodes are MERGEd, then edges, with endpoints required to exist in `best`; missing-endpoint edges are COUNTED AND SKIPPED, never stubbed. Edge MERGE keys on {edge_type, props} because props is part of edge identity (CTO 225614Z). An untyped-node check, a per-layer summary, a provenance manifest write, and the comp_detect TSGRAPH fold gate follow; rc is 0 only when untyped == 0 and the gate did not block.

stages_inferential: the FALLBACK pin only: latest_table_metadata() treats newest-*.metadata.json-by-mtime as HEAD, which the code's own comment marks RETIRED because mtime-newest can be an orphaned-commit artifact (CVO dc06744c6). It is inferential, it is NOT the active path this session (the marker resolved), and when it is taken the run says so.
stages_deterministic: the marker-driven pin, the pyiceberg StaticTable full-table read, and the snapshot-id capture
node dedup on (arn or node_id) keeping max snapshot_ts, with key_collisions counted
drop-and-rebuild under --force with a hard SystemExit on a surviving path
edge MERGE on {edge_type, props} with missing-endpoint edges counted and skipped

persistence.form: A Kuzu database at --db (default infra/aws/globgrph/kuzu_nessie_db), materialized by Kuzu as either a directory or a single file depending on version -- the wipe path handles both. Two tables: CloudNode(node_id PK, arn, node_type, name, layer, drift_class, source, snapshot_ts, props) and CloudEdge(FROM CloudNode TO CloudNode, edge_type, layer, snapshot_ts, props). A provenance manifest is written BESIDE the DB carrying source_kind=nessie, both snapshot ids, both metadata keys and their LastModified, the warehouse bucket/prefix, and node/edge counts.
persistence.evidence: DEFAULT_DB_PATH at kuzu_nessie_load.py:42; table DDL at :134-141; both-shapes wipe at :125-129; manifest fields at :213-229. Classified 'projection' rather than 'source' deliberately: every value it holds is read from the Iceberg tables, which remain the authority -- the DB is rebuilt from them and holds nothing that is not recoverable from the marker plus the warehouse. That is the exact opposite of its sibling derive_stitch.py, which DERIVES edges existing nowhere else and is therefore a source.

coverage.universe: Every row of graph_nodes and graph_edges at the pinned metadata_location -- full-table scans, not sampled, not filtered by layer or type.
coverage.denominator: PRINTED BY THE RUN ITSELF, and unusually completely: ICEBERG_READ nodes=<n> edges=<n> (rows read), NODES_DEDUP unique=<n> (from <n> rows, key_collisions=<n>), EDGES_WRITTEN written=<n> skipped_missing_endpoint=<n>, a per-layer LAYER <layer> nodes=<n> breakdown, and UNTYPED_NODES count=<n>. Every reported number carries what it is a count of, and the read-vs-written gap is visible rather than reconciled away.
explicitly_out: edges whose src_id or dst_id is not in the deduped node set -- COUNTED as skipped_missing_endpoint and dropped rather than stubbed, so the graph never gains a fabricated endpoint
node rows with an empty key (neither arn nor node_id) -- skipped by the `if not key: continue` guard, and these are NOT counted anywhere, so an all-empty-key batch would shrink the graph silently
any Iceberg commit newer than the marker's metadata_location -- by design, the pin is the point of consistency
the fold gate's own findings when it raises internally -- fail-open by explicit design
coverage.evidence: Print statements at kuzu_nessie_load.py:115-116, :143-144, :162-163, :202, :204-210. The empty-key skip is at :150-151 and is the one drop with no counter beside it -- read at source, not inferred.

key.identity_space: MIXED WITHIN ONE COLUMN BY DESIGN. The Kuzu primary key node_id is set to `arn if non-empty else node_id`, because comp_aws_cli keys EDGES by ARN while a node's own `id` is the short name with the ARN in a separate column. So the PK column holds ARNs for AWS-plane nodes and short names for everything else, and edge endpoints must be expressed in the same mixed space to match.
key.declared_mapping: Declared and justified in an inline comment at kuzu_nessie_load.py:145-149 ('the Kuzu PK is arn-if-present else node_id'), with the dedup rule (newest snapshot_ts wins per key) stated in the same block. The docstring's Schema section (:19-24) declares the column list but NOT this key rule -- the rule lives only in the implementation comment.
key.evidence: Key construction at :148; dedup and collision counting at :149-163. Rated UNKNOWN rather than stable or unstable ON PURPOSE: the code COUNTS key collisions (a same-key row disagreeing on node_id/node_type increments `collisions` and is reported), which means the instrument to answer this exists and prints on every run -- but I did not execute the loader, so I have no observed collision count for the live tables. The honest answer is that stability is MEASURABLE HERE AND UNMEASURED BY ME, not that it is fine.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: LOUD ALMOST EVERYWHERE, which makes this substrate materially safer than its sibling. Missing branch-head marker -> printed WARN: HEAD-ORACLE UNKNOWN plus an explicit fallback (the degrade ANNOUNCES itself). No metadata.json for a table prefix -> SystemExit with the prefix named. --force unable to remove the DB -> SystemExit rather than a MERGE into a half-wiped DB (this exact hazard was observed: 1967 nodes from a 1180-row table after a Windows file-lock rmtree failure). Edge endpoints missing -> counted and skipped, never stubbed. Untyped nodes -> OK/ERROR line and rc=1. A NEW un-baselined fold-gate finding -> BLOCKED, promotion halted, rc=1, with an audited COMP_DETECT_GATE_OVERRIDE escape. THE ONE FAIL-OPEN: comp_detect raising internally is caught by a bare `except Exception` at :253 which prints WARN: TSGRAPH fold gate could not run (<err>) and does NOT block -- deliberate and documented ('a gate crash must not block a valid graph'), and it PRINTS, so it is visible in a log. A SECOND, quieter one: _provenance.read_branch_head_marker swallows every failure into None, so 'marker absent', 'S3 unreachable' and 'unparseable JSON' are one value -- the caller still announces UNKNOWN, so the DEGRADE is distinguishable while its CAUSE is not.
silent_degrade_paths: an all-empty-key node batch would be skipped by the `if not key: continue` guard at :150-151 with no counter incremented -- the only uncounted drop in the file
comp_detect gate raising internally -> gate does not run, rc stays 0; visible only as a WARN line, so a caller reading rc alone sees a clean load with no gate
read_branch_head_marker's bare except collapses absent / unreachable / malformed into None -- the fallback is announced but the reason is lost
failure_mode.evidence: Read at source: WARN + fallback :105-107; SystemExit on no metadata :60-61; wipe hard-fail :130-131; edge skip :186-188; untyped rc :208-210, :257; fold gate block :244-251 and fail-open except :253-254; empty-key skip :150-151; _provenance.py:133-142 for the three-into-one None. ⛔ NOT EXERCISED, and named because the sibling card's row 7 WAS: I did not run this loader or force any of these branches. Its failure modes are read, not provoked. The one thing I did measure live is that the primary oracle RESOLVES (marker present, 02:11:47Z), so the announced-fallback path is not currently active.

verdict.why: This is the better-built of the two load-bearing writers and the card should say so plainly: it announces its own degrade instead of hiding it (HEAD-ORACLE UNKNOWN), hard-fails rather than proceeding on a partial wipe after that exact corruption was once observed, counts and reports every drop it makes instead of reconciling it away, keeps props in edge identity so distinct edges cannot collapse last-wins, and ends on a fold gate that actually HALTS promotion rather than warning. Its primary pin resolved live at carding. QUALIFIED, not SOUND, on three measured points, and the first is the one that will bite a reader: (1) DECLARATIVE DRIFT -- the module docstring at :10-18 still presents newest-metadata-by-mtime as THE pinning mechanism, while the code retired it to a fallback and its own inline comment cites the CVO finding that mtime-newest can be an orphaned-commit artifact; the docstring is what a reader meets first and it describes a mechanism that is no longer primary. (2) One uncounted drop: the empty-key guard at :150-151 is the single skip in the file with no counter beside it, in a file whose whole discipline is counting its skips. (3) The key space is mixed within one PK column by design and its stability is MEASURABLE by the collision counter the code already prints, but UNMEASURED here because I did not execute the loader -- key_is_stable is recorded as unknown rather than guessed. None of the three requires redesign; (1) is a documentation edit.
blocking_defects: docstring :10-18 documents the RETIRED mtime pin as primary while the code pins on the branch-head marker (declarative drift; owner 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps; a doc edit, not a code change)
empty-key node rows dropped at :150-151 with no counter, in a file that counts every other skip (coverage row)
key_is_stable UNKNOWN -- the collision counter exists and prints, but the loader was not executed by this carding lane (key row; resolvable by one run)
